stated: Fix the life-threatening crisis in our ambulance services by: Ending excessive handover delays for ambulances by increasing the number of staffed hospital beds to end degrading corridor care, and fixing social care. Publishing accessible, localised reports of ambulance response times. Creating an emergency fund to reverse closures of community ambulance stations and cancel planned closures where needed.

source.quote: Fix the life-threatening crisis in our ambulance services by: Ending excessive handover delays for ambulances by increasing the number of staffed hospital beds to end degrading corridor care, and fixing social care as set out in chapter 7. Publishing accessible, localised reports of ambulance response times. Creating an emergency fund to reverse closures of community ambulance stations and cancel planned closures where needed.

bearing_set.reason: Directly targets ambulance response times, hospital handover delays, and community station capacity — all core healthcare access indicators.
Fixing social care as a mechanism to end handover delays has a non-negligible direct bearing on social care access for older people, a key security-in-later-life indicator.

membership_note: Two clear bearings: O3 is the primary target (ambulance response, beds, station closures); O8 is a genuine secondary bearing because social care reform is explicitly named as part of the intervention — delayed discharge driven by social care gaps is the main driver of handover delays, so any real social care fix would materially improve O8 outcomes. No credible fiscal mechanism is specified with enough detail to separately score O12.
